name: ipmiutil
why: IPMI is a out-of-band management protocol running inside many servers, and this tool is the key to that hidden door.

brief.what_it_is: ipmiutil is a set of command-line IPMI server management utilities. It talks to the IPMI management controller in server hardware to read and set sensor values and thresholds, manage the System Event Log (SEL), open a serial-over-LAN (SOL) remote console, and handle power control and related tasks. The brew package installs 23 executables with names like isensor, isel, isol, iuser, iwdt, ipmiutil and ihealth. Output is text on the terminal. The SourceForge page says it also interprets vendor OEM sensor values automatically.
brief.why_it_exists: The project describes itself as an easy-to-use set of IPMI server management utilities, supporting multiple operating systems. Its SourceForge page also claims it is 'the only IPMI project tool that runs natively on Windows'. The page says it was formerly called panicsel.
brief.how_it_works: The pages I read did not explain the internals. The SourceForge page says Linux can run driverless, which makes it usable on boot media or embedded environments, and that Windows support uses native drivers. Beyond that I could not confirm the mechanism.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gave no install steps. The SourceForge description points to ipmiutil.sf.net for RPMs and other packages. Linux can run driverless, which the project says suits boot media and embedded systems. Windows is built natively and relies on its own drivers, which the project says sets it apart from other IPMI tools. I saw no account, runtime, or configuration steps.
brief.standout: The project claims to be the only IPMI tool that runs natively on Windows with its own drivers, and that it can run driverless on Linux from boot media. Both are the project's own claims, and I could not check them against the homepage or a README.
brief.status: SourceForge lists the project as maintained by three named developers, with a Last Update date of 2026-09-18, 1,155 downloads this week, and a registration date of 2004-08-05. The homepage itself showed no release or commit dates. The 2026 date looks unusual, so verify it before relying on it. Overall I would call it active, but I could not confirm that from source.
brief.caveats: I could not read a README. The homepage returned only a title and navigation, so the description above comes from the SourceForge project page. The brew package has no caveats. The project is BSD licensed, per SourceForge. Platforms listed are Linux, Windows, BSD, Solaris, macOS and HPUX. The SourceForge page also lists a note from users about the tool's usefulness, and the project's self-description may be marketing. The scout note's 'hidden door' framing is not a claim I could verify.
quotes: ipmiutil is an easy to use set of IPMI server management utilities.
The only IPMI project tool that runs natively on Windows.
It can run driverless in Linux for use on boot media or embedded environments.
Any IPMI values not yet recognized at least return the values, rather than just 'na' or Unknown.

judge.reason: It opens a little-known out-of-band hardware interface: inspect server sensors and event logs, reach a remote console, or control power without relying on the host OS.

entry.title: ipmiutil
entry.tldr: A suite of 23 command-line tools for talking to the hidden management controller inside server hardware: sensors, event logs, power, and a remote serial console.
entry.deeper_look:
Many servers contain a second, small computer called a baseboard management controller. It runs whether or not the main machine is on, and it speaks IPMI, a standard protocol for out-of-band management. ipmiutil is a set of command-line tools that talk to it. Per the project, they read and set sensor values and thresholds, manage the System Event Log, open a serial-over-LAN console, and handle power control and related tasks.

The package installs 23 executables, each with a narrow job. Names like isensor, isel, isol, iuser, iwdt and ihealth cover sensors, event log, serial console, users, watchdog timer and a health check. ipmiutil itself is the main entry point. Output is plain text on the terminal.

The project calls itself "an easy to use set of IPMI server management utilities" and says it was formerly called panicsel. It also says that IPMI values it does not yet recognize are returned anyway, "rather than just 'na' or Unknown." It claims Linux can run driverless, which suits boot media and embedded environments, and that on Windows it uses native drivers.

The idea underneath is out-of-band management: a machine you can inspect, reset or watch from a console even when its operating system is hung or absent. The tools are a way in to that layer. Be aware that you need a machine with an IPMI controller to see anything real.
entry.install:
brew install ipmiutil
Needs a machine with an IPMI-capable management controller (typically server hardware), or network access to one, for most commands to return anything useful.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the list of IPMI functions the main tool offers and its options.
Shows how to read sensor values and thresholds from the management controller.
Shows how to view or manage the System Event Log.

entry.whats_unique: It splits IPMI work into many small single-purpose tools, and the project says it runs natively on Windows and driverless on Linux. Both are the project's own claims.
entry.caveats: Without IPMI hardware most commands have nothing to talk to, and I could not read a README, so the commands here are limited to --help.
